domain_restrictions: d ranges over positive integers only
The product index i ranges over integers between a + 1 and b inclusive
If a equals b, the product is empty and equals 1
P_{a,b,r}(q) is interpreted as an element of the polynomial ring in q with integer coefficients when the claim says it belongs to Z[q]
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: For each fixed choice of integers a, b, r satisfying 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0, the finite product P_{a,b,r}(q), defined as the product over i from a + 1 to b of (1 minus q to the power r plus i) divided by (1 minus q to the power i), with empty product equal to 1, is a polynomial with integer coefficients in q if and only if for every positive integer d, floor((r + b) divided by d) minus floor((r + a) divided by d) is at least floor(b divided by d) minus floor(a divided by d).
quantifier_order: Fix integers a, b, r with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0
Define P_{a,b,r}(q) by the finite product over integers i from a + 1 to b, with empty product equal to 1
For every positive integer d, the stated floor-function inequality must hold
The claim is that the polynomial membership of P_{a,b,r}(q) is equivalent to that universal condition on d

variables.name: q
variables.role: indeterminate used to define the product

witness_dependencies: There is no existential witness in the statement; the condition is purely universal in d
The truth of the polynomial membership claim depends on checking the inequality for every positive integer d

statement_nl: Let a, b, r be integers with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0. Define P_{a,b,r}(q) := product_{i=a+1}^{b} ((1 - q^(r+i)) / (1 - q^i)), with empty product equal to 1. Then P_{a,b,r}(q) belongs to Z[q] if and only if for every positive integer d one has floor((r+b)/d) - floor((r+a)/d) >= floor(b/d) - floor(a/d).
